value.title: Assign, release, lineage and the directory view
value.summary: Roadmap 001 step s04. Seats take and leave roles with `pij directory assign` and `release`; every holder is recorded in lineage (seat, harness session, machine, from, to) on the governance branch, so it survives a store rebuild and other machines can read it; `pij close` ends a seat's assignment; and `pij directory` shows this project's roles and holders.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Plan 190 shipped the writer and `pij directory add`. Roles exist but nobody holds them except in the hand-kept HOLDERS.md. This plan adds holding: assign and release, lineage, the close hook, the directory view, and the rulings that touch assignment (C1 seat roles, C6 queue-drain hook, C13/req-26 window names). Lineage lives on the governance branch, written through the plan 190 writer, and the store indexes it (migration 0031 pointers plus migration 0032), so `pij directory` gives the same answer after a store rebuild (req-17).

sections.name: goals
value: A seat can take and leave a role with one verb each, and every holder is on record with its session and machine.
Lineage is on the governance branch, so a store rebuild or another machine sees the same holders.
Closing a seat ends its assignment without making close fail.
`pij directory` shows this project's roles and their holders and nothing from another project.

sections.name: non_goals
value: Sending to a role and the role queue (s05). This plan only exposes the hook s05 uses (C6).
Role templates and the core-role prompts (s03).
Outputs, memory verbs and routing (s06 to s08).
Starting seats: assign binds an existing live seat and never spawns one.

value.claim: Schemas. docs-system adds `pij/holders` (per role: rows of seat id, harness, harness session id, machine, instance key, from, to, assigned by, released by and why) and `pij/external` (req-16: dated entries for a seat borrowed from another project) under `.dd/schemas/pij/`, with pass and fail fixtures, and the writer's embedded schema copies (C9) include them.

Assign. `pij directory assign <role>[/<instance>] <seat> --why <text>` binds a live seat to an existing role: it appends a holder row to `community/roles/<id>/holders.dd.json` through the plan 190 writer (validate, build, `git commit --only`), records it in the store (migration 0032), and returns the commit and row. Assigning a second live seat to a one-holder role succeeds with a named warning (req-06). A role or seat that does not exist, or a tombstoned seat, refuses by name and writes nothing.

Seat roles (ruling C1). Assign also sets the seat's `seat_roles` row in the same store transaction as the assignment: `pa` for the role `pa`, `pm` for `pm` or any `pm-<n>` role, and `worker` for every other role; a prime is never re-roled. Release does not change seat_roles. A test shows the directory and seat_roles agree after assign.
value.receipt: 98863f6 store test + bccfc76 directory_http: seat_roles set in the assignment transaction, agree with the directory

value.claim: Release and close. `pij directory release <role>[/<instance>] <seat> --why <text>` closes the holder row (`to`, `released by`, why). `pij close <seat>` ends every open assignment the seat holds, recording `to` and the reason `close`. Close never fails because of the directory: if the writer refuses (no governance worktree, a foreign edit), the close still tombstones, the store keeps the end as pending, the close receipt says so by name, and the next directory write for that project flushes it.
value.receipt: bccfc76 directory_http: release; close ends holdings; refused end pending, named, flushed by the next write

value.claim: Queue-drain hook (ruling C6). Assign calls a registered after-assign hook with (project, role, instance, seat) after the commit lands, injected through the constructor (P3), with a no-op default. A test registers a hook and sees exactly one call per successful assign and none for a refused one. s05 will use it to drain the role queue.
value.receipt: bccfc76 directory_http: CountingHook, one call per successful assign, none for refused

value.claim: Window name (req-26, C16). On assign, the holder's tmux window is renamed `<project>:<role>`, or `<project>:<role>-<instance>` for a many-holder role, with one tmux launch per assign by absolute path through pij_core::program::launch, recorded by the spawn counter, not the control client (its read allow-list stays as S2 pinned it). A seat with no pane, or a rename failure, does not fail the assign; the receipt says so.
value.receipt: 87ad0d4: real-tmux rename test (counter +1) and directory_http window receipt, paneless note

value.claim: View (req-01). `pij directory` run inside a project lists that project's roles (id, title, kind, holders mode) and their live holders (seat, since, machine), plus pending close-ends, and nothing from another project; `--json` gives the same data. It reads the role and holder documents from the governance worktree in-process and the store; it launches nothing.
value.receipt: 87ad0d4 directory_http: per-project view, in-process (root::find, no launch)

value.claim: Rebuild (req-17). Deleting the store's directory rows (pointers, assignments, lineage) and rebuilding from the governance branch head gives byte-identical `pij directory --json` output, including closed holders' lineage.
value.receipt: 87ad0d4 directory_http: drop rows, rebuild from branch head, byte-identical --json

value.claim: External entries (req-16). `pij directory external add <seat-or-note> --from-project <slug> --why <text>` appends a dated entry to `community/external.dd.json` through the writer. Loans are not otherwise tracked.
Help. `pij directory --help` and `pij directory <verb> --help` print the verbs and their flags and exit 0, instead of `E-RS-ARG --help requires a value` (found in the wave B dogfood).
value.receipt: 7a067b4: help offline (CLI) and via daemon (shim), exit 0

value.claim: Cost. Assign costs one writer commit plus the window rename (about 10 launches: git 7, ddocs 2, tmux 1); release, external add and a close that ends an assignment each cost one writer commit (about 9); every launch is by absolute path, recorded by the spawn counter and covered by spawn_sites.rs; the view launches nothing; nothing runs on a timer. The backpressure cost row carries before and after readings.

Docs and states. docs/how/pij-rs-api.md documents the verbs and refusals; the pij skill's verb coverage and shim route tables carry them. In this PR: roadmap s04 goes to complete with its plan cell set to docs/plans/195-assign-lineage; req-01, req-06 and req-16 go to shipped; req-17 goes to shipped; c-store and c-verbs go to in-progress (later steps add verbs); c-orient goes to in-progress. All project docs validate clean.

Adopt (wave B dogfood F3). `pij directory add` for a role whose folder already exists without role.dd.json (a hand-written role with memory/INDEX.md, outputs/ and role.md) adopts the folder: it writes role.dd.json and its .dd.md, writes neither memory nor outputs files when those exist, and leaves role.md alone. E-RS-DIRECTORY-EXISTS fires only when role.dd.json exists, names that file and gives the next step; a batch names every role that already exists.
value.receipt: 87ad0d4 directory_http: adopt writes only role.dd.json and .dd.md; EXISTS names the file; batch names every role

value.claim: Foreign edits on written paths only (F4). The foreign-edit check covers only the paths the write will actually write, so adopting a role does not refuse over an edited memory/INDEX.md it leaves alone.
value.receipt: 87ad0d4 directory_http: an unstaged memory/INDEX.md edit stays and does not refuse the adopt

value.claim: Linked worktrees (F2). Project resolution matches a caller in a linked worktree to the project whose repo shares its common git dir, so a fleet-* worktree finds its project without --project. With no project for the repo, the refusal names the fix: `pij project create <name> --repo <path> --prime <seat>`.
value.receipt: 87ad0d4 directory_http: linked worktree resolves the project; unknown repo names pij project create ... --prime

value.title: Assign, release, close hook, view and rebuild
value.brief: AC2 to AC12. Coder. Migration 0032 (assignments and lineage index); the verbs through the plan 190 writer; seat_roles per C1; the C6 hook; the close path in crates/daemon/src/http/lifecycle.rs; the view; rebuild from the branch; window rename via the control client; help; docs; flips. Can start before phase 1 lands on the parts that don't parse holder documents. CS-4.

sections.name: research_context
sections.value: Code facts (2026-11-04, main 6ccd4d8): seats table in crates/store/migrations/0001_init.sql:15-36 (harness session serialised as `session`, crates/core/src/model.rs:348-376; machine is a read projection, not stored per row). seat_roles (seat, role, assigned_by, assigned_at) in 0004_orchestration.sql:48-53, written via crates/store/src/role_assertion.rs. Close: CLI crates/cli/src/lifecycle.rs:9-20 posts /v1/close; handler crates/daemon/src/http/lifecycle.rs:241-348 calls registry.tombstone_if_unchanged; publish_tombstone in crates/store/src/registry.rs:48-99 is the one path for close, reap and revive. Project resolution: project_and_repo in crates/daemon/src/http/directory.rs:331-380. Pointer rebuild: crates/daemon/src/community/pointer.rs:20-85 (from_branch_head). Directory argv is forwarded to the daemon parser (crates/cli/src/governance.rs:14-28, crates/daemon/src/http/directory.rs:55-115), which is why --help fails. Window name is set only at spawn (crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:1330-1337, crates/tmux/src/lib.rs:1528); the control client supports rename (crates/tmux/src/control.rs:595-598). Latest migration 0031; migrations registered by sqlx migrate! (crates/store/src/migrate.rs:38).

value.question: Where does lineage live? Recommended (used in this plan): a separate pij-written `roles/<id>/holders.dd.json`, not rows inside role.dd.json, so a human editing the role never collides with pij's lineage writes (the writer refuses foreign edits on its paths).

Wave B dogfood (docs-system job 6) is importing the hand-written roles and is expected to hit E-RS-DIRECTORY-EXISTS because each role already has memory/INDEX.md. Any writer fix it calls for (for example, adopting an existing role folder) is folded into this plan by pm-001 before phase 2 starts.

value.risk: A close blocked or slowed by a governance write.
value.mitigation: AC4: close never fails on the directory; pending ends are flushed by the next write.

value.risk: Lineage and the store disagree after a crash between commit and store write.
value.mitigation: The branch is the authority; rebuild (AC8) restores the store; persist before mutate (P9).

value.risk: Renaming a window confuses a human working in it.
value.mitigation: Only on assign, once; the name says what the seat does.

sections.name: execution_guardrails
value: Tests use scratch repos and a private daemon; never the live governance branch or the prod daemon.
Builds scoped with -p. Check `df -h /System/Volumes/Data` before a large build; stop and tell pm-001 under 25 GB. Reuse your existing target dir.
No `git add -A`, no `--no-verify`, never push refs/notes/*. No node_modules: TS proof is CI on the exact head.
One push per review round; no pushes after a PR is out for verdicts unless a verdict asks.
